    expect paginate(items, 1, 10) to return the first ten items
    expect paginate(items, 3, 10) to return an empty list

  Two details worth knowing:

  - Pages are counted from 1, so page 0 is rejected rather than treated as the first page.
  - The helper never copies the whole list: paginate(items, page, size) slices from (page - 1) * size, so asking for a page past the end costs
    nothing and returns an empty list. The caller decides whether an empty page is an error or just the end of the data.

  You don't need a database for either test; a plain array of twenty-five numbers is enough.

  What to do now

  1. Add the two cases to paginate.test.ts. Leave paginate.ts alone for now.
  2. Run npm test.
  3. Expect the second case to fail, because the helper throws past the last page today. That is the failure we want to see first.
  4. Paste the test file and the output here and I'll review it. Hold the commit; the tests and the fix go in together.

  One question to think about while you write it: the first case already proves slicing works, so why test a page past the end as well? Take a guess, even
  if you're unsure.
